title: Persian Herb, Lamb and Kidney Bean Stew with Dried Lime
summary: Lamb shoulder simmers with a mountain of slowly fried herbs, kidney beans and sour dried limes until tender and rich, served with fluffy rice and cool yoghurt.
equipment: large heavy casserole (Dutch oven, 5-6 litres) with lid

ingredients.item: boneless lamb shoulder, trimmed, cut into 3 cm pieces
fine sea salt or table salt
tin red kidney beans, drained and rinsed (about 240 g drained)
fresh flat-leaf parsley leaves and tender stems
fresh coriander leaves and tender stems
spring onions, including green tops (1 bunch)
saffron threads (about 20), crumbled into 2 tbsp hot water
basmati or other long-grain white rice
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Brown the lamb
steps.text: Season the lamb with the stew salt and pepper. Heat the 2 tbsp oil in the casserole over medium-high heat and brown the lamb in 2 batches for 6-8 min each, then set aside. Good colour on the meat builds a savoury base for the long simmer.

steps.title: Start the stew
steps.text: Lower the heat to medium and cook the onion for 8-10 min, until soft and golden at the edges. Stir in the turmeric for 30 s, then return the lamb and its juices with the 1 litre water, scraping up the browned bits. Bring to the boil, cover, lower the heat and simmer gently for 1 h.

steps.title: Soak the limes
steps.text: Meanwhile, soak the dried limes in warm water for 30 min, keeping them submerged with a small plate. Once softened, pierce each one 5-6 times with a fork so the sour juice can flow into the stew.

steps.title: Prepare the herbs
steps.text: Wash the herbs and spin them very dry. Chop the parsley and coriander very finely in the processor in batches, but chop the chives and spring onions by hand. Their hollow, juicy stems turn to mush in a processor.

steps.title: Fry the herbs patiently
steps.text: Heat the 4 tbsp herb oil in the frying pan over medium heat, add the chives and spring onions and stir for 2 min. Add the parsley and coriander, crumble in the fenugreek and cook for 18-20 min, stirring often, until very dark green and dry and green oil appears when you press them with a spoon. Turn the heat down if they begin to catch; this slow frying concentrates their flavour and colour, which defines the dish.

steps.title: Simmer until thick
steps.text: Once the lamb has had its first hour, stir in the fried herbs, beans and pierced limes, pushing the limes under the liquid. Cover and simmer gently for 1 h-1 h 15 min, stirring every 20 min, until the lamb is very tender and the stew is thick. If it looks watery, uncover for the last 15 min to let it reduce.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.text: About 30 min before the stew is ready, rinse the rice until the water runs clear. Put it in the saucepan with the 600 ml water and rice salt, bring to the boil, cover and cook on the lowest heat for 15 min, then rest for 10 min off the heat so the grains firm up and separate.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Press 2-3 of the softened limes with the back of a spoon to release their sour juice, then stir in the saffron water. Taste, adding lime juice if it needs more tang, and serve with the rice and yoghurt.

tips: A common mistake is under-frying the herbs; keep going until they are very dark and release green oil, or the stew will taste grassy rather than deep.
Spin the herbs completely dry first, since wet herbs steam rather than fry.
Do not squeeze every lime hard; pressing just 2-3 gives tang without too much bitterness.
The stew tastes even better the next day once the flavours settle.
storage: Cool within 2 hours and refrigerate for up to 3 days, or freeze the stew for up to 3 months. Reheat until piping hot (74°C), adding a splash of water if needed.
